test_title: PYST 77: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 25 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A cylindrical tank of radius 14 cm is full of water. If 616 litres of water are drawn out, then the water level in the tank is dropped by ______ m. (Take π = (22/7) )
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Drop in height (h) = Volume ÷ Base Area = V ÷ πr²

⇒ h = (616 × 1000) ÷ ((22/7) × 14 × 14) cm

⇒ h = 616000 ÷ 616 = 1000 cm

⇒ h = 10 m

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the cylindrical tank, r = 14 cm

Volume of water drawn out, V = 616 litres

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

1 Litre = 1000 cm³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/868ecac0e39d366d76031c0cbdf523119dc00c6313d3653d08f1836c12541f22.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the drop in water level be h.

⇒ Volume drawn out = 616 × 1000 = 616000 cm³

⇒ V = πr²h

⇒ 616000 = (22/7) × 14 × 14 × h

⇒ 616000 = 22 × 2 × 14 × h

⇒ 616000 = 616 × h

⇒ h = 616000 ÷ 616

⇒ h = 1000 cm

⇒ Since 1 m = 100 cm, h = 1000 ÷ 100 = 10 m

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Formulas

Volume = πr²h | Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh | Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(r+h).

Volume Conversions

1 Litre = 1000 cm³ | 1 m³ = 1000 Litres | 1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³.

Direct Proportion in Cylinders

For a uniform cross-section tank, the volume drawn or added is directly proportional to the change in height (ΔV = Base Area × Δh).
